newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open slightly higher, climb.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open slightly higher, climb.

text.p: French shares opened slightly higher on Thursday and extended their gains in early trading, after Wednesday's sharp selloff.
At 0930 GMT the CAC-40 index of blue chip stocks was up 0.76 percent or 19.56 points at 2,602.73 in over one billion francs of volume.

On Wednesday the Paris bourse closed 3.63 percent lower, its second big drop of the week after the combined left won the first round of France's parliamentary election. The second and final round will be held on Sunday.
"This is a market of excesses," one trader said. "There have been sharp changes that didn't mean very much."
But dealers said that despite Thursday's rebound, many investors were remaining cautious because of the market's instability in recent sessions.
"We are correcting yesterday's excess in a reasonable volume but we'll have to wait and see," another trader said. "We opened higher yesterday, too."
Dealers said Thursday's buying was mostly either bottom-fishing or short-covering after the market's big drops on Monday and Wednesday.

The market was again influenced by election result rumours, this time by talk a poll by the Swiss newspaper La Tribune de Geneve set for release this evening on the internet would show the right well placed ahead of Sunday's runoff.

French bond futures were lower, but above their lows for the day and holding at technical support above 128. June PIBOR futures were up five basis points at 96.28, regaining most of the ground lost on Wednesday.
